title: Russian Culture in a Digital World
description: New media’s impact on social, cultural, and political development of Russian society. Russian art, values and ideologies, state power, nationalism, and democracy.
notes: Taught in English. Native speakers of Russian will not receive credit for taking lower division courses in Russian except with advance approval from the department. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.

title: Russian Culture, Identity, and Society
description: Examines Russian culture and identity from Imperial times to today. Students analyze primary sources exploring autocracy, religion, gender, empire, nature, ecology, and memory while investigating how cultural practices shape and reflect evolving definitions of Russian national identity.
notes: Taught in English

title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
description: Advanced grammar and stylistics; intensive writing practice; reports based on outside reading.  Course uses language acquisition skills to help students understand cultural differences and develop a global perspective.
notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian. No credit will be given for

title: Russian for Business Communication
description: Russian business communication to include business letters, reports, presentations. Topics include banking, business etiquette, international trade, marketing.
notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.

title: Heroes and Villains: Russian Literature of the Nineteenth Century
description: Nineteenth century Russian literature in translation. Prose fiction in cultural and historical context of Russian Empire to include works by Dostoevsky, Pushkin, Tolstoy, Turgenev.
notes: Taught in English with readings in English.

title: Russian Literature of the Twentieth Century
description: Twentieth century Russian literature including works by Zamyatin, Pasternak, Akhmatova, Solzhenitsyn.
notes: Taught in English with readings in English.

title: Russian and East European Cinema
description: Through study of films from 1950s to post-Soviet times, major concerns of East Europeans are addressed through cinema. Interrelationships among cinematic traditions of Russia, Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, and former Yugoslavia/Balkans.
notes: Taught in English.

title: Russian Through Media
description: Russian stylistics and discourse grammar in context. Emphasis on communicative skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Students work with Internet materials, newspapers, magazines, and excerpts from Russian and Soviet films.
notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.

title: Russian Civilization
description: Russian civilization through literary texts, visual art, music, and film. Relationships between art and politics, art and national identity, art of the fantastic and doublespeak, art of postcommunism and postmodernism.
notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.

title: Russian and East European Jewish Culture
description: Russian and East European Jewish culture from 1900s to present. How literature written in Russian, Polish, Czech, Lithuanian, German by writers of Jewish origin as well as visual arts and cinema reflect changing problem of Jewish national identity.
notes: Taught in English.

title: Russian Internship
description: Practical work experience in a field related to Russian studies. Work done under joint direction of activity sponsor and instructor. Approved international internships may count towards international experience requirement for major.
notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.

notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.

title: Translation
description: Comparison of Russian and English through translation of a variety of texts from Russian to English and from English to Russian.
notes: Taught in Russian. No credit will be given for lower division courses taken after successfully completing any upper division Russian course taught in Russian.
